## Project Summary
 
Current rates of species extinctions are at least 100 times higher than background rates (Ceballos et al., 2015). To address this, national and international policies have made the conservation of biological diversity a priority (UN CBD, 2010). However, conservation funding is insufficient (McCarthy et al., 2012). Therefore, managers face the very real challenge of deciding how to allocating financial resources to effective conservation actions that maximize the conservation return-on-investment (Murdoch et al., 2007).
 
A useful tool for guiding decisions about resource allocation is Cost-Effectiveness Analysis (CEA). In essence, a CEA simply determines the cost-efficiency of each project based on its cost, benefits and the likelihood of success. By ranking projects based on their cost-efficiency, it is possible to identify projects that are predicted to provide the biggest returns on investment. In the conservation sector, a systematic CEA tool, called the Project Prioritization Protocol (PPP), has been developed to inform decisions about the allocation of funding among endangered species recovery plans (Joseph et al., 2009). Under the PPP, the cost-efficiency of each project (i.e., recovery plan for a species) is assessed based on estimates of 
1) the long-term cost of all required management actions to recover a species (i.e., cost), 
2) the probability that the management will successfully secure the species from extinction (i.e., success), and 
3) the benefit of management to the species (i.e., benefit). 
 
The output is a list of projects ranked in decreasing order based on their efficiency: at the top of the list are the recovery plan projects that will provide the biggest conservation return on investment. The cumulative cost is calculated moving down the list, and all projects that can be afforded for the specified budget are included in a portfolio of funded projects.
 
A large and growing number of regional, state and national bodies are employing PPP to guide conservation decisions. For example, the PPP is currently used by governments to improve endangered species funding allocation decisions in New Zealand (Bennett et al., 2014; Joseph et al., 2009) and in New South Wales in Australia (Brazill-Boast et al., in prep; Szabo et al., 2009). A demonstration of the tool is now available for the United States of America (Iacona et al., in prep). However, a general concern about using Cost-Effectiveness Analysis to inform conservation management decisions is that the quality of the data on cost, benefit, and probability of success are too poor to provide good guidance. Though these data may be estimated from experiments or predictive models, estimates are often based on expert opinion due to a lack of time or resources for rigorous data collection and analysis. As a result, managers may hesitate to accept the output of a cost-effectiveness analysis because of concerns that the recommendations are not robust to uncertainty in the data. But, whether estimated from experiments, models or expert opinion, no data are perfect. The important question is not whether data is good quality, but whether the guidance for the resource allocation decision is robust to uncertainty in the data.  
 
**The objective of this study** is to answer the question “are decisions about resource allocation for endangered species management using the PPP robust to data uncertainty, and do they generate useful and sensible decision guidance”. This will be accomplished using endangered species listed under the USA Endangered Species Act as a case study, as part of a larger collaboration (Iacona et al., in prep). This study will comprise part of Stephanie Avery-Gomm's PhD thesis
 

## Methods
 
This analysis has occurs in 3 stages. First, code provided by Dr. Gwen Iacona extracts data from Recovery Plans (unique_plan_num), and performs a cost-effectiveness analysis to generate a recommended portfolio of funded species for a range of budgets (Iacona et al., in prep). Second, I  simulate uncertainty in the estimates of cost, benefit, and success (feasibility), and then re-run the cost-effectiveness analysis iteratively to determine how introducing uncertainty changes the portfolios of funded species. Finally, I will characterize the changes in terms of how uncertainty would change the decision. 
 
#### 1. Cost-Effectiveness Analysis 
Data on 1351 species listed as endangered under the USA Endangered Species Act has been extracted from 545 published Recovery Plans (unique_plan_num). For each, the cost is estimated as the sum total of all listed management actions in the recovery plan, divided by 50 to give the *annual cost* of recovery. Values for Benefit and Success for each species was assigned based on the Recovery Prioirty Number assigned by the USFWS (See RPN_Benefit_Success_Taxonomy.R). See Iacona et al., (in prep) and code package provided by Gwen Iacona for more details on data collection. Within this R Markdown file are a draft description of the study (draft, as of March 5, 2017) and the code for the analysis. The package 'Checkpoint,' which is part of the Reproducible R Toolkit from Microsoft has been used: it retrieve all necessary packages according to the date & versions specified in the code. 
 
For lack of better alternatives, Recovery Priority Numbers were interpreted in the following ways to provide estimates of Benefit with Management, Benefits without Management and Taxonomic Weighting. The trailing 'C' in the original Recovery Priority Numbers indicates 'Conflict.'For more information about the Recovery priority Numbers see https://www.fws.gov/endangered/esa-library/pdf/1983_LPN_Policy_FR_pub.pdf
 
- Taxonomic Weighting (subspecies, species, monotypic genus)

- Recoverability Potential (low, high) was converted to a numeric value (0.5, 1) and used as a value to represent the BENEFIT (probability of persitence) WITH MGMT. USFWS has assigned 'low' Recoverability Potential to species where biology and ecological factors are poorly understood, threats are poorly understood/pervasive/not easily alleviated, and management will be intensive, and success is uncertain (bc involves poorly understood or experimental techniques). A species with low recoverability potential will not benefit very much from having it's Recovery Plan funded, so benefit with management) is also low. Species with a 'high' scoring, are the opposite. 

- Degree of Threat (low, med, high) represents the magnitude and the immediacy of the threat, and we use this to represent the BENEFIT (probability of persitence) WITHOUT MANAGEMENT.  This was converted to a numeric value (1 minus 0.33, 1 minus 0.66, 1 minus 0.99 == 0.67, 0.34, 0.01). The interpretation of this is that a species facing HIGH Degree of threat (large magnitude, and immediacy) will benefit more to have it's threat mitigated by mangement than a species that is facing low magnitude, non-immediate threats. We chose NOT to use the listed threat status to indicate Benefit of Management as these can be politically motivated and rarely up to date. 

The IMPACT (overall Benefit) of a project on the species probability of persistence is the difference between the BENEFIT WITH MGMT and BENEFIT WITHOUT MGMT. ** unfortunately, unique_plan_num with low degree of threat and low recoverability potential end up having negative IMPACT (Benefit) so these were forced to 0.001. And so that this made sense throughout, Benefit without Management was forced from 0.67 to 0.499.

## Preparing B, S, Co data and removing outliers (i.e., Recovery Plans (unique_plan_num) with Co = 0). 

Preparation of the file to run the uncertainty analysis requires combining several intermediate products.
    Inputs
     - AllPPPOutput.csv: final output from PPP analysis, which provides cost at the level of Recovery Plan (identified based on unique_plan_num)
     - draft_b: an intermediate product produced just for me prior to creation of Data2.csv in the GenerateBenefits.R function of the PPP analysis. data_b tells me what sp_vip_codes were included in the analysis and is used to link data on Benefits from the species level RPN file
     - RPNs-for-plan_id-and-sp_vip_code-combos-NAs-imputed.csv: The *first* intermediate file produced by RPN_Benefit_Success_Taxonomy3.R. This file contains needed information on B, B_with_without_Mgmt at the level of sp_vip_code.
    
    Output
    - dataSpp: contains sp_vip_code level Benefit and Success data & unique_plan_id level cost data. excludes unusable data
     
```{r load_RPN_B_S_T_for_1350_sps_vip_codes}

# Same file from RPN Program file in shared SESYNC folder, used by Gwen to produce final AllPPPOutput.csv.
RPNdata <- read.csv("./data/Run 20 - Sept 2020/RPNs-for-plan_id-and-sp_vip_code-combos-NAs-imputed.csv")
    str(RPNdata)

    # Verify class factor
    class(RPNdata$sp_vip_code)
    class(RPNdata$plan_id)

    # Check levels
    length(unique(RPNdata$unique_plan_num)) # 596 unique_plan_num before exclusions
    length(unique(RPNdata$plan_id)) # 1350 sp_vip_code before exclusions
     
    # Trim any plan level information - it is not relevant here *we need only to match based on sp_vip_code
    RPNdata <- RPNdata %>%
            mutate(cannot_impute = ifelse(is.na(RPN_Benefit), 1, 0)) %>% # ID those species without Benefit data
            mutate(unique_plan_num = plan_id) %>% # simplifies things later
            select(-unique_plan_num, -action_species, -plan_id, -plan_lead_region, -plan_title)

    # Verify that there are no sp_vip_codes with >1 RPN_Benefit value
    count_RPN_benefit_sp_vip_code <- RPNdata %>%
            group_by(sp_vip_code) %>%
            summarise(Benefit_in_sp_vip_code = length(unique(RPN_Benefit)))
             # View(count_RPN_benefit_sp_vip_code)
       
  
    # IMPORTANT NOTES ABOUT HOW RPN for USFWS PPP scaled NoRPNs imputed.csv WAS CREATED:
    #     The code that created this output (called RPN_Benefit_Success_Taxonomy3.R) joins species level RPN data to Data2.csv by = "sp_vip_code" and "plan_id" (which is later renamed to unique_plan_num)
    #     New variable "USFWS_RPN_Available" added, and species assigned as 1/0 where 1 = Y and 0 = N.
    #     For sps without RPNs which have membership in multi-species recovery plans I will assign AVERAGE Benefit_without_Mgmt and Benefit_with_Mgmt. If a sp_vip_code is imputed but belongs in multiple plans, I made sure there was a consistent RPN across all case (just took the average and applied manually)
    #     Data from this file are used to mutate 'Benefit'. RPN_Success and RPN_Success_runif are added (not related to RPN data)
    #     Then for each Data2$plan_id values of Benefit, Benefit_without_Mgmt and Benefit_with_Mgmt are summed.
    #     Verify the summed Benefit still = Benefit_with_Mgmt - Benefit_without_Mgmt
```

```{r read_draft_b}

# Read in draft_b, which is an intermediate step in the “GenerateBenefits.R” script written in at line 20 (directly before it was used to calculate plan level benefits from species id level benefits). So, this shows exactly the right number of sp_vip_codes and unique_plan_id as have contributed to the Benefit and Costs in AllOutput.csv. None of the Benefit data has been imputed.
    draft_b <- read.csv("./data/Run 20 - Sept 2020/draft_b.csv")
    
    # Add a “unique plan num” column so it can be merged with AllOutput.
    # str(draft_b)
    draft_b <- draft_b %>%
        mutate(unique_plan_num = plan_id) %>%
        select(sp_vip_code, unique_plan_num, everything(), -plan_id, -plan_title)
    
    draft_b$unique_plan_num<- as.character(draft_b$unique_plan_num)
    draft_b$unique_plan_num<- as.factor(draft_b$unique_plan_num)
    # str(draft_b)
```

```{r merge_B_with_without_Mgmt_from_RPNdata_to_draft_b}

# First, Verify there is agreement between data from RPNdata & draft_b (nothing hinky with levels)
    test <- left_join(draft_b, RPNdata, by = "sp_vip_code")
    test2 <- test %>%
        mutate(MATCHB = ifelse(RPN_Benefit.x == RPN_Benefit.y, TRUE, FALSE),
               MATCHT = ifelse(RPN_TaxoWeighting.x == RPN_TaxoWeighting.y, TRUE, FALSE),
               MATCHS = ifelse(RPN_Success.x == RPN_Success.y, TRUE, FALSE))
        # subsets should have 0 rows
        dim(filter(test2, MATCHB == FALSE))
        dim(filter(test2, MATCHS == FALSE))
        dim(filter(test2, MATCHT == FALSE))

# Trim duplicate colnames from RPN_Benefit (or draft_b, doesn't matter)
   RPNdata2<- RPNdata %>%
       select(-RPN_Benefit, -RPN_TaxoWeighting, -RPN_Success)

# Merge draft_b (which includes Recovery Plan data) with missing RPNdata (rpn, Conflict, Degree of threat, recoverability potential, Benefit_with/without_Mgmt)
   draft_b <- left_join(draft_b, RPNdata2, by = "sp_vip_code")
   
    draft_b$sp_vip_code<- as.character(draft_b$sp_vip_code)
    draft_b$sp_vip_code<- as.factor(draft_b$sp_vip_code)
```

```{r prep_for_uncertainty}
# For Uncertainty analyses using the rBeta distribution values need to be scaled so that they fall between 0.12 - 0.88 (i.e., (x*0.78)+0.12). This scales, renames draft_b to dataSpp and adds B, S & W columns

# Rename draft_b and plan level Co, S, W, CE etc (save for later verification)
    dataSpp <- draft_b %>%
    mutate(plan_CE = CE, 
           plan_B = B,
           plan_S = S,
           plan_W = W,
           plan_Co = Co) %>%
    select(-CE, -B, -S, -W, -Co)
    
    # Feasibility is a random number. Must be scaled 
        dataSpp$S <-(draft_b$RPN_Success_runif/max(draft_b$RPN_Success_runif)*0.76)+0.12
        
    # Taxonomic Distinctiveness is not used here
        dataSpp$W <-(draft_b$RPN_TaxoWeighting/max(draft_b$RPN_TaxoWeighting)*0.76)+0.12
    
    # Cost is still at Recovery Plan level, so we carry it over (undoing the step above where we reassign. They should match.
        dataSpp$Co <- dataSpp$plan_Co
    
        # Benefit is the impact of the management
        # The difference in the prob of persistence after mangement (aka recoverability potential) minus without management (aka degree of threat) must be forced to 0.001 in six cases, where it is otherwise negative by our choice of values. Regardless of this change, these projects have very small benefit. 
        forceto0.001 <- dataSpp %>% mutate(ISSUE = Benefit_with_Mgmt - Benefit_without_Mgmt) %>% 
            filter(ISSUE < 0)
        ISSUE<-unique(forceto0.001$unique_plan_num) #600101 600084 400306 600331 600252

        dataSpp<- dataSpp %>%
            mutate(Benefit_without_Mgmt = ifelse(unique_plan_num %in% ISSUE, 0.499, Benefit_without_Mgmt))
        
        dataSpp<- dataSpp %>%
            mutate(B = Benefit_with_Mgmt- Benefit_without_Mgmt) %>%
            mutate(B = (B/max(B)*0.76)+0.12) # this scales the 6 cases with issues which WERE Benefit = 0.001 to 0.12 for the sake of uncertainty analysis. This means the results of my analysis are not realistic, but of course, we already knew that. 
        
        dataSpp<- dataSpp %>%
            mutate(B_without_Mgmt = Benefit_without_Mgmt) %>%  # these are not scaled - no need to unless uncertainty is being introduced. 
            mutate(B_with_Mgmt = Benefit_with_Mgmt)
        
       
    
    # Arrange in order of increasing unique_plan_num
    dataSpp <- arrange(dataSpp, unique_plan_num)
    # str(dataSpp)
 
    # Save!
    write.csv(dataSpp,file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/dataSpp.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

The Cost-Effectiveness Analysis will be conducted as described by the Project Prioritization Protocol (Joseph et al., 2009). The efficiency, Ce, of each project, i, will be calculated as: 
 
Ei=(Bi*Si)/Coi 
 
Where i is an index for the identity of the project and
Ci is the cost of the project, i, 
Bi is the benefits to the species of the project, i
Si is probability of success of the project, i
 
Next, all projects will be ranked by their cost-efficiency, CE, to provide a ranked ordered list of projects that can be considered for funding.  Whether a project is included in the funded portfolio depends on how far down the list it is, and how big the budget is. The cumulative cost (CumSum) is calculated moving down the ranked list of projects, and all projects that can be afforded for the specified budget are included in a portfolio of funded projects (Outcome = 1). The funding threshold is the point at which the specified budget runs out because the cumulative project costs exceed it. The baseline portfolio refers to the result where no uncertainty has been introduced into the estimates of Cost, Benefit, and Success. 
 
 
#### 2. Simulating Uncertainty 
To explore how robust the portfolio of funded projects is to uncertainty, the first step is to introduce uncertainty into the three parameters in the cost-efficiency analysis (i.e., cost, benefit, and success) for each project (i.e., species recovery plan). Next, project efficiencies are recalculated and projects are re-ranked to determine what the funded portfolio of projects will be for each level of uncertainty tested.  
 
For each uncertainty treatment (i.e., High, Medium, and Low), random variables will be generated from distributions of the cost, benefit, success, for each species project. To generate the distributions for each variable I will use the original estimate of cost, benefit, and success as the mean and uncertainty treatments will have Low, Medium and High variance around the mean.  
For benefits and success the probability density function of the Beta distribution is an appropriate distribution because it is bounded between 0 and 1. The benefit and success, uncertainty treatments will introduce High (variance = 0.01), Medium (variance = 0.005) and Low (variance = 0.001) variance around the mean (e.g., Table 2).  For cost, I will use a normal distribution. For cost estimates uncertainty treatments will introduce High (sd=mean x 0.20), Medium (sd=mean x 0.1) and Low (sd=mean x 0.05) variance around the mean.
 
 ### ** PROBABLY HAVE TO FIX HOW BENFIT IS REPRESENTED - HOW WE EXPLAIN HOW WE COME TO IT ** ### 
 
The following code shows the rBeta function, and how levels of uncertainty (variance) can be viewed and interpreted. Note that categorical levels of Degree of Threat based on each species Recovery Priority Number have been converted into a continuous index of Benefit. Similarly, the categorical levels of 'Recoverability Potential' have been converted into a continuous index of Feasibility (referred to according to the syntax of the PPP as Success). Also shown are chosen variance levels for Cost. 
 
```{r rBeta, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# Load rBeta function for Beta Distribution (applies to B & S)
source("./R.functions/rBeta.R")

# Visualize using code from Cran rbeta help file, including limit cases.
x <- seq(0, 1, length = 21)
dbeta(x, 1, 1)
pbeta(x, 1, 1)

pl.beta <- function(a,b, asp = if(isLim) 1, ylim = if(isLim) c(0,1.1)) {
  if(isLim <- a == 0 || b == 0 || a == Inf || b == Inf) {
    eps <- 1e-10
    x <- c(0, eps, (1:7)/16, 1/2+c(-eps,0,eps), (9:15)/16, 1-eps, 1)
  } else {
    x <- seq(0, 1, length = 1025)
  }
  fx <- cbind(dbeta(x, a,b), pbeta(x, a,b), qbeta(x, a,b))
  f <- fx; f[fx == Inf] <- 1e100
  matplot(x, f, ylab="", type="l", ylim=ylim, asp=asp,
          main = sprintf("[dpq]beta(x, a=%g, b=%g)", a,b))
  abline(0,1,     col="gray", lty=3)
  abline(h = 0:1, col="gray", lty=3)
  legend("top", paste0(c("d","p","q"), "beta(x, a,b)"),
          col=1:3, lty=1:3, bty = "n")
  invisible(cbind(x, fx))
}
```

#### 3. Treatments
Recalling the objective is to answer the question “are decisions about resource allocation for endangered species management using the PPP robust to data uncertainty, and do they generate useful and sensible decision guidance” it is necessary to explore how the introduction of uncertainty into different parameters of the CE analysis affect the outcome. 
 
Here, I use loops and lists to run the CE analysis on all combinations of parameters (parameters = B, S, Co). First I set up a simulation dataframe (sim_df or SimSet, depending) with the following combinations. Each are run separately, and the results are collated at the end:
 
0. Baseline (no uncertainty) from above
1. Benefit & Success (Feasibility) & Cost
2. Benefit & Success (Feasibility)
3. Benefit & Cost
4. Success & Cost 
5. Benefit
6. Success (Feasibility)
7. Cost
 
There will be a total of 63 treatment combinations: 3 levels of uncertainty, 3 budget levels and 7 combinations of parameters with introduced certainty **NOTE: Plus the baseline - not yet done, but Gwen's base analysis should provide that because it's all the same data**


 
#### 4. Characterize the Influence of Uncertainty 
For each of the 7 parameter combinations, I run through the 9 different uncertainty treatment interatively. In each iteration I re-calculate the Recovery Plan cost efficiency (CE) with the simulated variables. As before, projects will be ranked in order of decreasing project efficiency, and the cumulative costs will be calculated, moving down the list. All those projects that can be afforded for the specified budget will be in the portfolio of funded projects (Outcome = 1). This process will be repeated 100 times for each treatment, and each time the portfolio of funded species will be saved. 
 
The ultimate goal of the CE Analysis is to provide decision makers with a ranked list of projects, and the suggestion to start at the top. But, uncertainty in estiamtes of Benefit, Success or Cost can change the rank order of projects, and given a set budget, the identify and number of projects in the funded portfolio. 
 
Here, I characterize the influence of that uncertainty on the recommendations of a Cost Efficiency Analysis in three ways: 
 
1. Performance of Funded Portfolios under Uncertainty. For each treatment, I will estimate the performance of the funded portfolio and determine at what levels of uncertainty the performance changes, or if it is consistent across uncertainty treatments (i.e., robust). This will help to explore which parameters (i.e., B, S, or Co) drive change and what different levels of uncertainty mean. **NOTE: Funded portfolio likely most sensitive to uncertainty in Co as it is in the denominator of the CE equation!**
    i) Number of Species put on the 'pathway to recovery' ( # of funded plans x the # species per plan) **NOTE: This is necessary because some plans are MultiSpecies Recovery Plans (unique_plan_num), and could represent up to 59 species**
    ii) Performance (cumulative sum of BS for all funded projects x the # of species in the plan ) **NOTE: Not using Ayesha formulae for saved sps because we cannot estimate Probability of Persistence**
    
2. Probability of Funding - For each treatment, I will estimate the probability of inclusion (i.e., out of 100 runs) of a project is in the funded portfolio. If the funded portfolios are robust to data uncertainty, then there will be consistency in the inclusion or exclusion of projects across uncertainty treatments. If the decisions are not robust, then projects will drop in and out of the funded portfolio when parameter estimates are varied. **NOTE: Expectation is that High uncertainty will strongly influence the identity of the species in the funded pool.**

3. Number of Recovery Plans (unique_plan_num) funded Under Uncertainty - exploring the relationship between budget and MeanFunded and different levels of Unceratinty (in BCo) and 100 different budget levels (using SimSet100)

Here is the code for the 7  parameter combinations (8 if you include the unfinished, unnecessary (?) Baseline treatment). Only the Benefit & Success (Feasibility) & Cost is included in the RMarkdown, as an example.

If the simulations have already been run (correctly) read in the output and prob_fund_results csvs rather than rerunning. 
The relevant files must be in ./output/ directory.

```{r Baseline_Treatments, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE, message=FALSE}

###### Baseline_Treatment ###############################

# Clear the slate of earlier datasims
rm(datasim)

# BE SURE that dataSpp which is basis of _probfund dataframe is arranged in order!
dataSpp <- dataSpp %>%
    arrange(unique_plan_num)

    # Set up the empty dataframes for each summary result
    Baseline_results <- list()
    Baseline_mean_funded <- as.numeric()
    Baseline_sd_funded <- as.numeric()
    Baseline_mean_perform <- as.numeric()
    Baseline_sd_perform <- as.numeric()
    Baseline_probfund <- data.frame(unique_plan_num = unique(dataSpp$unique_plan_num))  # UPDATED Oct 17 2017

    # 2-level loop: Simulate uncertainty to Benefit & Cost and calculate CEA for species at multiple Budget levels
    # Define number of loop

        loops <- 100

        for (t in 1:nrow(sim_df_baseline)){
            ##  Give a 'progress bar' to see where you are in the loop
            # cat('sim_df BSCo',t,'/',nrow(sim_df),'\n')

            results_df <- list()
            results_funded <- numeric()
            results_perform <- numeric()
            results_probfund <- data.frame(unique_plan_num = unique(dataSpp$unique_plan_num))

            for(i in 1:loops) {
                # DON'T add uncertainty to B & S at species level
                datasim <- dataSpp %>%
                        mutate(B_without_Mgmt= Benefit_without_Mgmt,
                               B_with_Mgmt= Benefit_with_Mgmt,
                               S = S) ## RECALL S is RUNIF

                # Get back to B&S&Co at plan level
                datasim <- datasim %>%
                    group_by(unique_plan_num) %>%
                    summarise(
                        B = sum(B, na.rm = TRUE),
                        S = mean(S, na.rm = TRUE),
                        Co = mean(Co, na.rm = TRUE),
                        SpeciesInPlan = mean(SpeciesInPlan, na.rm = TRUE),
                        B_without_Mgmt = sum(B_without_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE),
                        B_with_Mgmt = sum(B_with_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE))

                # Convert Co for total plan to ANNUAL costs (divide by 50)
                datasim <- mutate(datasim, Co=(Co/50))

                # DON'T ADD uncertainty to Co at plan level
                # datasim <- datasim %>%
                #     rowwise() %>%
                #     mutate(Co = rnorm(1, mean = Co, sd = Co*sim_df[t,"UCo"]))
                # print(head(datasim)) # << CHECKS THAT relevant parameters are changing consistent with

                # Calculate cost efficiency and outcome for each plan
                datasim <- datasim %>%
                    mutate(CE=((B*S)/Co)) %>%
                    arrange(desc(CE)) %>%
                    mutate(CumSum=cumsum(Co)) %>%
                    mutate(Outcome=ifelse(CumSum>=sim_df[t,"UBudget"], 0, 1)) %>%
                    arrange(unique_plan_num)

                # How many SPECIES FUNDED per treatment?
                # Save number of plans funded for each budget and treatment
                results_funded[i] <- sum(datasim$Outcome*datasim$SpeciesInPlan)

                # What is the PERFORMANCE of each treatment? 
                ## Performance = [benefit with mgmt - benefit without mgmt | Outcome == 1] + [benefit without mgmt FOR ALL PROJECTS]" (this changed June 17 2018 after feedback from Mike Runge on equation error!)
                benefit_without_management <- sum(datasim$B_without_Mgmt)
                # print(sum(datasim$B*datasim$S*datasim$Outcome)) # << For uncertainty treatments, CHECK that benefit without management changes
                results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim$B*datasim$S*datasim$Outcome), benefit_without_management)
                results_df[[i]] <- datasim

                # WHAT IS PROBABILITY EACH PROJECT WILL BE FUNDED?
                results_probfund[,as.character(i+1)] <- datasim$Outcome

                }

            Baseline_mean_funded[t] <- mean(results_funded)
            Baseline_sd_funded[t] <- sd(results_funded)
            Baseline_mean_perform[t] <- mean(results_perform)
            Baseline_sd_perform[t] <- sd(results_perform)
            Baseline_results[[t]] <- results_df

            Baseline_probfund[,t+1] <- rowSums(results_probfund[,2:ncol(results_probfund)])/loops
        }

       
        
        # 1 & 2) Create dataframe to hold results for mean +/- SD # Species Funded/Performance
            # Numb Funded Species & Performance for each treatment
            Baseline_output <- data.frame(Treatment=rep("Baseline", nrow(sim_df_baseline)),
                                     SimSet=sim_df_baseline$SimSet,
                                     UBS=sim_df_baseline$UBS,
                                     UCo=sim_df_baseline$UCo,
                                     UBudget=sim_df_baseline$UBudget,
                                     MeanFunded=round(Baseline_mean_funded,1),
                                     SDFunded=round(Baseline_sd_funded,2),
                                     MeanPerform=round(Baseline_mean_perform,1),
                                     SDPerform=round(Baseline_sd_perform,2))

            # Reattach names to the Baseline_probfund
            names(Baseline_probfund) <- c("unique_plan_num", as.character(Baseline_output$SimSet))

            # Test if the cumsum of all projects where prob.fund == 1.0
            # test_probfund has unique_plan_num and the probabilities (from 0 to 1)
            costs<-select(datasim, unique_plan_num, Co)
            xcosts <- left_join(Baseline_probfund, costs, by = "unique_plan_num")
            test <- xcosts %>%
                mutate(NAH = ifelse(NAH < 1, 0, Co),
                       NAM = ifelse(NAM < 1, 0, Co),
                       NAL = ifelse(NAL < 1, 0, Co))

            colSums(select(test, NAH:Co)) # Sum for always funded projects shouldn't exceed H budget = 30 mil, M budget = 15 min, L budget = 7.5 mil

            
            # Taking datasim from the Baseline scenario, create a vector of unique_plan_num that includes ONLY recovery items in the funded portfolio (Outcome == 1)
            funded_unique_plan_num_H <- Baseline_probfund %>%
                select(unique_plan_num, NAH) %>%
                filter(NAH > 0) %>%
                droplevels()
            funded_unique_plan_num_H <- funded_unique_plan_num_H$unique_plan_num
            funded_unique_plan_num_H
            
            funded_unique_plan_num_M <- Baseline_probfund %>%
                select(unique_plan_num, NAM) %>%
                filter(NAM > 0) %>%
                droplevels()
            funded_unique_plan_num_M <- funded_unique_plan_num_M$unique_plan_num
            funded_unique_plan_num_M
            
            funded_unique_plan_num_L <- Baseline_probfund %>%
                select(unique_plan_num, NAL) %>%
                filter(NAL > 0) %>%
                droplevels()
            funded_unique_plan_num_L <- funded_unique_plan_num_L$unique_plan_num
            funded_unique_plan_num_L

        # 3) Calculate which species are always/never funded funded for each uncertainty/budget treatment
            # For each Treatment (column), subset where value >0.99 and count rows for Always.
            # For each Treatment (column), subset where value == 0 and count rows for Never.
            # df[df==""]<-NA
            Baseline_always <- Baseline_probfund[,2:ncol(Baseline_probfund)]
            Baseline_always[Baseline_always > 0.99] <- 1
            Baseline_always[Baseline_always <= 0.99] <- NA
            Baseline_always <- cbind(Baseline_probfund[,1], Baseline_always)

            Baseline_never <- Baseline_probfund[,2:ncol(Baseline_probfund)] # Error in colSums(Baseline_never[, -1], na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric
            Baseline_never[Baseline_never != 0.00] <- NA
            Baseline_never[Baseline_never == 0.00] <- 1
            Baseline_never <- cbind(Baseline_probfund[,1], Baseline_never)

            Baseline_sometimes <- Baseline_probfund[,2:ncol(Baseline_probfund)] # Error in colSums(Baseline_never[, -1], na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric
            Baseline_sometimes[Baseline_sometimes == 0.00] <- NA
            Baseline_sometimes[Baseline_sometimes > 0.99] <- NA
            Baseline_sometimes[!is.na(Baseline_sometimes)] <- 1
            Baseline_sometimes <- cbind(Baseline_probfund[,1], Baseline_sometimes)

            # How many species, for each treatment are always/never funded? Add each parameter treatment (B, Co, BCo etc), as it is completed.
            Baseline_probfund_results<- data.frame(NULL)
            Baseline_always<- colSums(Baseline_always[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
            Baseline_sometimes<- colSums(Baseline_sometimes[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
            Baseline_never<- colSums(Baseline_never[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)

            Baseline_probfund_results<-rbind(Baseline_always, Baseline_sometimes, Baseline_never)
            # datatable((Baseline_probfund_results))


            
            
# system("say Baseline loop is finished running!")

# Write files so this doesn't always need to be rerun:
    # write.csv(datasim, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/datasim.Baseline.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    # write.csv(Baseline_probfund_results, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Baseline_probfund_results.csv", row.names = TRUE)
    # write.csv(Baseline_probfund, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Baseline_probfund.csv", row.names = TRUE)
    # write.csv(Baseline_output, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Baseline_output.csv", row.names = FALSE)

################ End Baseline_Treatment ################
```

###### Benefit / Success / Cost
```{r BSCo_Treatments, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE, message=FALSE, include = FALSE}

###### BSCo_Treatment ###############################
# Clear the slate of earlier datasims
rm(datasim)

# BE SURE that dataSpp which is basis of _probfund dataframe is arranged in order!
dataSpp <- dataSpp %>%
    arrange(unique_plan_num)


# Set up the empty dataframes for each summary result
BSCo_results <- list()
BSCo_mean_funded <- as.numeric()
BSCo_sd_funded <- as.numeric()
BSCo_mean_perform <- as.numeric()
BSCo_sd_perform <- as.numeric()
BSCo_probfund <- data.frame(unique_plan_num = unique(dataSpp$unique_plan_num))  # UPDATED Oct 17 2017


# 2-level loop: Simulate uncertainty to Benefit & Cost and calculate CEA for species at multiple Budget levels
loops <-100 # Define number of loop

for (t in 1:nrow(sim_df)){
    ##  Give a 'progress bar' to see where you are in the loop
    # cat('sim_df BSCo',t,'/',nrow(sim_df),'\n')

    ## Create place to store results
    results_df <- list()
    results_funded <- numeric()
    results_perform <- numeric()
    results_probfund <- data.frame(unique_plan_num = unique(dataSpp$unique_plan_num))  # UPDATED Oct 17 2017

        for(i in 1:loops) {

        # Add uncertainty to B&S at species level. For benefit, uncertainty is introduced to B_with/without_Mgmt, then B is calculated
        # datasim <- dataSpp %>%
        #     mutate( B_without_Mgmt = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$B_without_Mgmt), dataSpp$B_without_Mgmt, sim_df[t,"UBS"]),
        #             B_with_Mgmt    = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$B_with_Mgmt), dataSpp$B_with_Mgmt, sim_df[t,"UBS"]),
        #             S              = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$S), dataSpp$S, sim_df[t,"UBS"])) %>%
        #     mutate(B = B_with_Mgmt - B_without_Mgmt)

        datasim <- dataSpp %>%
            mutate( B_without_Mgmt = B_without_Mgmt,
                    B_with_Mgmt    = B_with_Mgmt,
                    S              = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$S), dataSpp$S, sim_df[t,"UBS"])) %>%
            # mutate(B = B_with_Mgmt - B_without_Mgmt) %>% # delete this
            mutate(B = rBeta(1:length(B), B, sim_df[t,"UBS"]))

        # Get back to B&S&Co at plan level
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            group_by(unique_plan_num) %>%
            summarise(
                B = sum(B, na.rm = TRUE),
                S = mean(S, na.rm = TRUE),
                Co = mean(Co, na.rm = TRUE),
                SpeciesInPlan = mean(SpeciesInPlan, na.rm = TRUE),
                B_without_Mgmt = sum(B_without_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE), #**changed Oct 17**##
                B_with_Mgmt = sum(B_with_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE)) #**changed Oct 17**##

        # Convert Co for total plan to ANNUAL costs (divide by 50)
        datasim <- mutate(datasim, Co=(Co/50))

        # Add uncertainty to Co at plan level
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            rowwise() %>%
            mutate(Co = rnorm(1, mean = Co, sd = Co*sim_df[t,"UCo"]))

        # print(head(datasim)) #  << CHECKS THAT relevant parameters are changing

        # Calculate cost efficiency and outcome for each plan
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            mutate(CE=((B*S)/Co)) %>%
            arrange(desc(CE)) %>%
            mutate(CumSum=cumsum(Co)) %>%
            mutate(Outcome=ifelse(CumSum >= sim_df[t,"UBudget"], 0, 1)) %>%
            arrange(unique_plan_num)

        # HOW MANY SPECIES FUNDED per treatment?
            # Save number of plans funded for each budget and treatment
            results_funded[i] <- sum(datasim$Outcome*datasim$SpeciesInPlan)

        # WHAT IS PERFORMANCE of treatment?
            # Performance = [benefit with mgmt - benefit without mgmt | Outcome == 1] + [benefit without mgmt FOR ALL PROJECTS]
            # B_without_mgmt applies to all recovery plans
                benefit_without_management <- sum(datasim$B_without_Mgmt)
            # B_with_mgmt calculations should apply only to the projects that were in the funded (7.5M, 15M, 30M) portfolio from the baseline portfolios, respectively. 
                    # So LOW budget  sim_df[t] == 3, 6, 8
                    # So MED budget  sim_df[t] == 2, 5, 8
                    # So HIGH budget  sim_df[t] == 1, 4, 7
          
                if (t %in% c(1, 4, 7)) { # We are in a HIGH BUDGET sim_df loop
                    
                    datasim_subset <- datasim %>%
                        filter(unique_plan_num %in% funded_unique_plan_num_H)
                    #print(sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)) 
                    results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)   

                    } else if (t %in% c(2, 5, 8)) { # We are in a MED BUDGET sim_df loop
                    
                    datasim_subset <- datasim %>%
                        filter(unique_plan_num %in% funded_unique_plan_num_M)
                    # print(sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)) 
                    results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)   

                
                    } else if (t %in% c(3, 6, 9)) { # We are in a LOW BUDGET sim_df loop
                    
                    datasim_subset <- datasim %>%
                        filter(unique_plan_num %in% funded_unique_plan_num_L)
                    #print(sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)) 
                    results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)   

                    } else {
                      stop("STOP! Something is wrong with the performance!")
                    }
        
        # Save each datasim as a list
        results_df[[i]] <- datasim
        
                
        # WHAT IS PROBABILITY EACH PROJECT WILL BE FUNDED? (check budget for always funded proj doesn't exceed budget)
        results_probfund[,as.character(i+1)] <- datasim$Outcome                                                        ########

                # Here we make sure that the cum cost of each funded profolio does not exceed the budget level
                x <- datasim %>%
                 group_by(Outcome) %>%
                 summarise(sum = sum(Co))
                x2 <- ifelse(x$sum[2] > sim_df[t,"UBudget"], "OH NO", "OK")
                troubleshoot2 <- data.frame(loopi = i, loopt = t, check = x2)
                troubleshoot <- rbind(troubleshoot,troubleshoot2)

        }

    BSCo_mean_funded[t] <- mean(results_funded)
    BSCo_sd_funded[t] <- sd(results_funded)
    BSCo_mean_perform[t] <- mean(results_perform)
    BSCo_sd_perform[t] <- sd(results_perform)
    BSCo_results[[t]] <- results_df
    BSCo_probfund[,t+1] <- rowSums(results_probfund[,2:ncol(results_probfund)])/loops
}


# 1 & 2) Create dataframe to hold results for mean +/- SD # Species Funded/Performance
# Numb Funded Species & Performance for each treatment
BSCo_output <- data.frame(Treatment=rep("BSCo", nrow(sim_df)),
                          SimSet=sim_df$SimSet,
                          UBS=sim_df$UBS,
                          UCo=sim_df$UCo,
                          UBudget=sim_df$UBudget,
                          MeanFunded=round(BSCo_mean_funded,1),
                          SDFunded=round(BSCo_sd_funded,2),
                          MeanPerform=round(BSCo_mean_perform,1),
                          SDPerform=round(BSCo_sd_perform,2))

        # Reattach names to the BSCo_probfund
        names(BSCo_probfund) <- c("unique_plan_num", as.character(BSCo_output$SimSet))


         # Test if the cumsum of all projects where prob.fund == 1.0
            # test_probfund has unique_plan_num and the probabilities (from 0 to 1)
            costs<-select(datasim, unique_plan_num, Co)
            xcosts <- left_join(BSCo_probfund, costs, by = "unique_plan_num")
            test <- xcosts %>%
                mutate(LLH = ifelse(LLH < 1, 0, Co),
                       LLM = ifelse(LLM < 1, 0, Co),
                       LLL = ifelse(LLL < 1, 0, Co),
                       MMH = ifelse(MMH < 1, 0, Co),
                       MMM = ifelse(MMM < 1, 0, Co),
                       MML = ifelse(MML < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHH = ifelse(HHH < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHM = ifelse(HHM < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHL = ifelse(HHL < 1, 0, Co))

            colSums(test) # Sum for always funded projects shouldn't exceed H budget = 30 mil, M budget = 15 min, L budget = 7.5 mil

# 3) Calculate which species are always/never funded funded for each uncertainty/budget treatment
# For each Treatment (column), subset where value >0.99 and count rows for Always.
# For each Treatment (column), subset where value == 0 and count rows for Never.
# df[df==""]<-NA
BSCo_always <- BSCo_probfund[,2:ncol(BSCo_probfund)]
BSCo_always[BSCo_always > 0.99] <- 1
BSCo_always[BSCo_always <= 0.99] <- NA
BSCo_always <- cbind(BSCo_probfund[,1], BSCo_always)

BSCo_sometimes <- BSCo_probfund[,2:ncol(BSCo_probfund)]
BSCo_sometimes[BSCo_sometimes == 0.00] <- NA
BSCo_sometimes[BSCo_sometimes > 0.99] <- NA
BSCo_sometimes[!is.na(BSCo_sometimes)] <- 1
BSCo_sometimes <- cbind(BSCo_probfund[,1], BSCo_sometimes)

BSCo_never <- BSCo_probfund[,2:ncol(BSCo_probfund)] # Error in colSums(BSCo_never[, -1], na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric
BSCo_never[BSCo_never != 0.00] <- NA
BSCo_never[BSCo_never == 0.00] <- 1
BSCo_never <- cbind(BSCo_probfund[,1], BSCo_never)

# How many species, for each treatment are always/never funded? Add each parameter treatment (B, Co, BCo etc), as it is completed.
BSCo_probfund_results<- data.frame(NULL)
BSCo_always<- colSums(BSCo_always[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
BSCo_sometimes<- colSums(BSCo_sometimes[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
BSCo_never<- colSums(BSCo_never[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
BSCo_probfund_results<-rbind(BSCo_always, BSCo_sometimes, BSCo_never)
datatable((BSCo_probfund_results))
datatable(BSCo_probfund)

# system("say B S Co loop is finished running!")

# # Write files so this doesn't always need to be rerun:
write.csv(datasim, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/one.of.the.datasim.BSCo.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(BSCo_probfund_results, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/BSCo_probfund_results.csv", row.names = TRUE)
write.csv(BSCo_output, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/BSCo_output.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(BSCo_probfund, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/BSCo_probfund.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```

```{r BCo_Treatments, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE, message=FALSE,  include = FALSE}
        #     # Performance = [benefit with mgmt - benefit without mgmt | Outcome == 1] + [benefit without mgmt FOR ALL PROJECTS]
        # 
        #     benefit_without_management <- sum(datasim$B_without_Mgmt)
        #     # print(sum(datasim$B*datasim$S*datasim$Outcome)) # << CHECKS THAT benefit without management changes
        #     results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim$B*datasim$S*datasim$Outcome), benefit_without_management)
        #     results_df[[i]] <- datasim

            # WHAT IS PERFORMANCE of treatment?
            # Performance = [benefit with mgmt - benefit without mgmt | Outcome == 1] + [benefit without mgmt FOR ALL PROJECTS]
            # B_without_mgmt applies to all recovery plans
                benefit_without_management <- sum(datasim$B_without_Mgmt)
            # B_with_mgmt calculations should apply only to the projects that were in the funded (7.5M, 15M, 30M) portfolio from the baseline portfolios, respectively. 
                    # So LOW budget  sim_df[t] == 3, 6, 8
                    # So MED budget  sim_df[t] == 2, 5, 8
                    # So HIGH budget  sim_df[t] == 1, 4, 7
          
                if (t %in% c(1, 4, 7)) { # We are in a HIGH BUDGET sim_df loop
                    
                    datasim_subset <- datasim %>%
                        filter(unique_plan_num %in% funded_unique_plan_num_H)
                    #print(sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)) 
                    results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)   

                    } else if (t %in% c(2, 5, 8)) { # We are in a MED BUDGET sim_df loop
                    
                    datasim_subset <- datasim %>%
                        filter(unique_plan_num %in% funded_unique_plan_num_M)
                    #print(sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)) 
                    results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)   

                
                    } else if (t %in% c(3, 6, 9)) { # We are in a LOW BUDGET sim_df loop
                    
                    datasim_subset <- datasim %>%
                        filter(unique_plan_num %in% funded_unique_plan_num_L)
                    #print(sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)) 
                    results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)   

                    } else {
                      stop("STOP! Something is wrong with the performance!")
                    }
        
        # Save each datasim as a list
        results_df[[i]] <- datasim
        
        # WHAT IS PROBABILITY EACH PROJECT WILL BE FUNDED? (check budget for always funded proj doesn't exceed budget)
        results_probfund[,as.character(i+1)] <- datasim$Outcome

    }

        BCo_mean_funded[t] <- mean(results_funded)
        BCo_sd_funded[t] <- sd(results_funded)
        BCo_mean_perform[t] <- mean(results_perform)
        BCo_sd_perform[t] <- sd(results_perform)
        BCo_results[[t]] <- results_df
        BCo_probfund[,t+1] <- rowSums(results_probfund[,2:ncol(results_probfund)])/100
    }

    # 1 & 2) Create dataframe to hold results for mean +/- SD # Species Funded/Performance
        # Numb Funded Species & Performance for each treatment
        BCo_output <- data.frame(Treatment=rep("BCo", nrow(sim_df)),
                                 SimSet=sim_df$SimSet,
                                 UBS=sim_df$UBS,
                                 UCo=sim_df$UCo,
                                 UBudget=sim_df$UBudget,
                                 MeanFunded=round(BCo_mean_funded,1),
                                 SDFunded=round(BCo_sd_funded,2),
                                 MeanPerform=round(BCo_mean_perform,1),
                                 SDPerform=round(BCo_sd_perform,2))

        # Reattach names to the BCo_probfund
        names(BCo_probfund) <- c("unique_plan_num", as.character(BCo_output$SimSet))

# Test if the cumsum of all projects where prob.fund == 1.0
            # test_probfund has unique_plan_num and the probabilities (from 0 to 1)
            costs<-select(datasim, unique_plan_num, Co)
            xcosts <- left_join(BCo_probfund, costs, by = "unique_plan_num")
            test <- xcosts %>%
                mutate(LLH = ifelse(LLH < 1, 0, Co),
                       LLM = ifelse(LLM < 1, 0, Co),
                       LLL = ifelse(LLL < 1, 0, Co),
                       MMH = ifelse(MMH < 1, 0, Co),
                       MMM = ifelse(MMM < 1, 0, Co),
                       MML = ifelse(MML < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHH = ifelse(HHH < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHM = ifelse(HHM < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHL = ifelse(HHL < 1, 0, Co))

            colSums(test) # Sum for always funded projects shouldn't exceed H budget = 30 mil, M budget = 15 min, L budget = 7.5 mil

    # 3) Calculate which species are always/never funded funded for each uncertainty/budget treatment
        # For each Treatment (column), subset where value >0.99 and count rows for Always.
        # For each Treatment (column), subset where value == 0 and count rows for Never.
        # df[df==""]<-NA
        BCo_always <- BCo_probfund[,2:ncol(BCo_probfund)]
        BCo_always[BCo_always > 0.99] <- 1
        BCo_always[BCo_always <= 0.99] <- NA
        BCo_always <- cbind(BCo_probfund[,1], BCo_always)

        BCo_sometimes <- BCo_probfund[,2:ncol(BCo_probfund)]
        BCo_sometimes[BCo_sometimes == 0.00] <- NA
        BCo_sometimes[BCo_sometimes > 0.99] <- NA
        BCo_sometimes[!is.na(BCo_sometimes)] <- 1
        BCo_sometimes <- cbind(BCo_probfund[,1], BCo_sometimes)

        BCo_never <- BCo_probfund[,2:ncol(BCo_probfund)] # Error in colSums(BCo_never[, -1], na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric
        BCo_never[BCo_never != 0.00] <- NA
        BCo_never[BCo_never == 0.00] <- 1
        BCo_never <- cbind(BCo_probfund[,1], BCo_never)

        # How many species, for each treatment are always/never funded? Add each parameter treatment (B, Co, BCo etc), as it is completed.
        BCo_probfund_results<- data.frame(NULL)
        BCo_always<- colSums(BCo_always[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
        BCo_sometimes<- colSums(BCo_sometimes[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
        BCo_never<- colSums(BCo_never[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
        BCo_probfund_results<-rbind(BCo_always, BCo_sometimes, BCo_never)
        # datatable((BCo_probfund_results))


system("say B Co loop is finished running!")

# Write files so this doesn't always need to be rerun:
    write.csv(datasim, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/one.of.the.datasim.BCo.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    write.csv(BCo_probfund_results, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/BCo_probfund_results.csv", row.names = TRUE)
    write.csv(BCo_output, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/BCo_output.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    write.csv(BCo_probfund, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/BCo_probfund.csv", row.names = TRUE)

########### End BCo_Treatment ####################
```

```{r SCo_Treatments, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE, message=FALSE,  include = FALSE}
                # Add uncertainty to S at species level. For benefit, uncertainty is introduced to B_with/without_Mgmt, then B is calculated
        datasim <- dataSpp %>%
            mutate( B_without_Mgmt = B_without_Mgmt,
                    B_with_Mgmt =    B_with_Mgmt,
                    S =              rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$S), dataSpp$S, sim_df[t,"UBS"]))
            # mutate(B = B_with_Mgmt - B_without_Mgmt) # delete this

        # Get back to B&S&Co at plan level
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            group_by(unique_plan_num) %>%

                B = sum(B, na.rm = TRUE),
                S = mean(S, na.rm = TRUE),
                Co = mean(Co, na.rm = TRUE),
                SpeciesInPlan = mean(SpeciesInPlan, na.rm = TRUE),
                B_without_Mgmt = sum(B_without_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE), #**changed Oct 17**##
                B_with_Mgmt = sum(B_with_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE)) #**changed Oct 17**##

        datasim <- mutate(datasim, Co=(Co/50))

        datasim <- datasim %>%
            rowwise() %>%
            mutate(Co = rnorm(1, mean = Co, sd = Co*sim_df[t,"UCo"]))

        # print(head(datasim)) #  << CHECKS THAT relevant parameters are changing

        # Calculate cost efficiency and outcome for each plan
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            mutate(CE=((B*S)/Co)) %>%
            arrange(desc(CE)) %>%
            mutate(CumSum=cumsum(Co)) %>%
            mutate(Outcome=ifelse(CumSum >= sim_df[t,"UBudget"], 0, 1)) %>%
            arrange(unique_plan_num)

        # HOW MANY SPECIES FUNDED per treatment?

                      stop("STOP! Something is wrong with the performance!")
                    }

        # WHAT IS PROBABILITY EACH PROJECT WILL BE FUNDED? (check budget for always funded proj doesn't exceed budget)
        results_probfund[,as.character(i+1)] <- datasim$Outcome                                                        ########

        SCo_mean_perform[t] <- mean(results_perform)
        SCo_sd_perform[t] <- sd(results_perform)

        SCo_never[SCo_never != 0.00] <- NA
        SCo_never[SCo_never == 0.00] <- 1
        SCo_never <- cbind(SCo_probfund[,1], SCo_never)
```

```{r B_Treatments, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE, message=FALSE, include = FALSE}
                    results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim_subset$B*datasim_subset$S), benefit_without_management)   

                    } else {
                      stop("STOP! Something is wrong with the code!")
                    }
                
        # Save each datasim as a list
        results_df[[i]] <- datasim
        
        # WHAT IS PROBABILITY EACH PROJECT WILL BE FUNDED? (check budget for always funded proj doesn't exceed budget)
            results_probfund[,as.character(i+1)] <- datasim$Outcome
            }

        B_mean_funded[t] <- mean(results_funded)
        B_sd_funded[t] <- sd(results_funded)
        B_mean_perform[t] <- mean(results_perform)
        B_sd_perform[t] <- sd(results_perform)
        B_results[[t]] <- results_df
        B_probfund[,t+1] <- rowSums(results_probfund[,2:ncol(results_probfund)])/100
        }

    # 1 & 2) Create dataframe to hold results for mean +/- SD # Species Funded/Performance
        # Numb Funded Species & Performance for each treatment
        B_output <- data.frame(Treatment=rep("B", nrow(sim_df)),
                                 SimSet=sim_df$SimSet,
                                 UBS=sim_df$UBS,
                                 UCo=sim_df$UCo,
                                 UBudget=sim_df$UBudget,
                                 MeanFunded=round(B_mean_funded,1),
                                 SDFunded=round(B_sd_funded,2),
                                 MeanPerform=round(B_mean_perform,1),
                                 SDPerform=round(B_sd_perform,2))

        # Reattach names to the B_probfund
        names(B_probfund) <- c("unique_plan_num", as.character(B_output$SimSet))

        # Test if the cumsum of all projects where prob.fund == 1.0
            # test_probfund has unique_plan_num and the probabilities (from 0 to 1)
            costs<-select(datasim, unique_plan_num, Co)
            xcosts <- left_join(B_probfund, costs, by = "unique_plan_num")
            str(xcosts)
            test <- xcosts %>%
                mutate(LLH = ifelse(LLH < 1, 0, Co),
                       LLM = ifelse(LLM < 1, 0, Co),
                       LLL = ifelse(LLL < 1, 0, Co),
                       MMH = ifelse(MMH < 1, 0, Co),
                       MMM = ifelse(MMM < 1, 0, Co),
                       MML = ifelse(MML < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHH = ifelse(HHH < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHM = ifelse(HHM < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHL = ifelse(HHL < 1, 0, Co))
            test<- select(test, everything(), -unique_plan_num)

            str(test)
            colSums(test) # Sum for always funded projects shouldn't exceed H budget = 30 mil, M budget = 15 min, L budget = 7.5 mil
            #        LLH        LLM        LLL        MMH        MMM        MML        HHH        HHM        HHL         Co 
            #   28685296   14067660    5372464   27231297   12633052    4985093   22357382   11878735    4512179 1686759883 
            
            
    # 3) Calculate which species are always/never funded funded for each uncertainty/budget treatment
        # For each Treatment (column), subset where value >0.99 and count rows for Always.
        # For each Treatment (column), subset where value == 0 and count rows for Never.
        # df[df==""]<-NA
        B_always <- B_probfund[,2:ncol(B_probfund)]
        B_always[B_always > 0.99] <- 1
        B_always[B_always <= 0.99] <- NA
        B_always <- cbind(B_probfund[,1], B_always)

        B_sometimes <- B_probfund[,2:ncol(B_probfund)] # Error in colSums(Co_never[, -1], na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric
        B_sometimes[B_sometimes == 0.00] <- NA
        B_sometimes[B_sometimes > 0.99] <- NA
        B_sometimes[!is.na(B_sometimes)] <- 1
        B_sometimes <- cbind(B_probfund[,1], B_sometimes)

        B_never <- B_probfund[,2:ncol(B_probfund)] # Error in colSums(B_never[, -1], na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric
        B_never[B_never != 0.00] <- NA
        B_never[B_never == 0.00] <- 1
        B_never <- cbind(B_probfund[,1], B_never)

        # # check data
        # head(B_always)
        # str(B_always)
        #
        # head(B_never)
        # str(B_never)

        # How many species, for each treatment are always/never funded? Add each parameter treatment (B, Co, BCo etc), as it is completed.
        B_probfund_results<- data.frame(NULL)
        B_always<- colSums(B_always[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
        B_sometimes<- colSums(B_sometimes[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
        B_never<- colSums(B_never[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
        B_probfund_results<-rbind(B_always, B_sometimes, B_never)
        datatable((B_probfund_results))

system("say B loop is finished running!")

# Write files so this doesn't always need to be rerun:
write.csv(datasim, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/one.of.the.datasim.B.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(B_probfund_results, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/B_probfund_results.csv", row.names = TRUE)
write.csv(B_output, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/B_output.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(B_probfund, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/B_probfund.csv", row.names = TRUE)

################ End B_Treatment ################
```

```{r S_Treatments, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE, message=FALSE, include = FALSE}
    # 2-level loop: Simulate uncertainty to Benefit & Cost and calculate CEA for species at multiple Budget levels
loops <-100 # Define number of loop

    for (t in 1:nrow(sim_df)){

                # Add uncertainty to S at species level. For benefit, uncertainty is introduced to B_with/without_Mgmt, then B is calculated
        datasim <- dataSpp %>%
            mutate( B_without_Mgmt = B_without_Mgmt,
                    B_with_Mgmt =    B_with_Mgmt,
                    S =              rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$S), dataSpp$S, sim_df[t,"UBS"]))
            # %>% mutate(B = B_with_Mgmt - B_without_Mgmt) %>% # delete this

        # Get back to B&S&Co at plan level
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            group_by(unique_plan_num) %>%

                B = sum(B, na.rm = TRUE),
                S = mean(S, na.rm = TRUE),
                Co = mean(Co, na.rm = TRUE),
                SpeciesInPlan = mean(SpeciesInPlan, na.rm = TRUE),
                B_without_Mgmt = sum(B_without_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE), #**changed Oct 17**##
                B_with_Mgmt = sum(B_with_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE)) #**changed Oct 17**##

        # print(head(datasim)) #  << CHECKS THAT relevant parameters are changing

        # Calculate cost efficiency and outcome for each plan
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            mutate(CE=((B*S)/Co)) %>%
            arrange(desc(CE)) %>%
            mutate(CumSum=cumsum(Co)) %>%
            mutate(Outcome=ifelse(CumSum >= sim_df[t,"UBudget"], 0, 1)) %>%
            arrange(unique_plan_num)

        # HOW MANY SPECIES FUNDED per treatment?
            # Save number of plans funded for each budget and treatment
            results_funded[i] <- sum(datasim$Outcome*datasim$SpeciesInPlan)

        # # WHAT IS PERFORMANCE of treatment?
        #     # Save performance of the funded portfolio
        #     # Performance = [benefit with mgmt - benefit without mgmt | Outcome == 1] + [benefit without mgmt FOR ALL PROJECTS]
        #     benefit_without_management <- sum(datasim$B_without_Mgmt)
        #     # print(sum(datasim$B*datasim$S*datasim$Outcome)) # << CHECKS THAT benefit without management changes
        #     results_perform[i] <- sum(sum(datasim$B*datasim$S*datasim$Outcome), benefit_without_management)
        #     results_df[[i]] <- datasim
            
            # WHAT IS PERFORMANCE of treatment?
            # Performance = [benefit with mgmt - benefit without mgmt | Outcome == 1] + [benefit without mgmt FOR ALL PROJECTS]
            # B_without_mgmt applies to all recovery plans
                benefit_without_management <- sum(datasim$B_without_Mgmt)
            # B_with_mgmt calculations should apply only to the projects that were in the funded (7.5M, 15M, 30M) portfolio from the baseline portfolios, respectively. 
                    # So LOW budget  sim_df[t] == 3, 6, 8
                    # So MED budget  sim_df[t] == 2, 5, 8

        # WHAT IS PROBABILITY EACH PROJECT WILL BE FUNDED? (check budget for always funded proj doesn't exceed budget)
        results_probfund[,as.character(i+1)] <- datasim$Outcome                                                        ########

            }

        S_mean_funded[t] <- mean(results_funded)
        S_sd_funded[t] <- sd(results_funded)
        S_mean_perform[t] <- mean(results_perform)
        S_sd_perform[t] <- sd(results_perform)

        S_probfund[,t+1] <- rowSums(results_probfund[,2:ncol(results_probfund)])/100
        }

        # Reattach names to the S_probfund
        names(S_probfund) <- c("unique_plan_num", as.character(S_output$SimSet))

        # Test if the cumsum of all projects where prob.fund == 1.0
            # test_probfund has unique_plan_num and the probabilities (from 0 to 1)

            xcosts <- left_join(S_probfund, costs, by = "unique_plan_num")

                       HHH = ifelse(HHH < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHM = ifelse(HHM < 1, 0, Co),
                       HHL = ifelse(HHL < 1, 0, Co))

            colSums(test) # Sum for always funded projects shouldn't exceed H budget = 30 mil, M budget = 15 min, L budget = 7.5 mil

    # 3) Calculate which species are always/never funded funded for each uncertainty/budget treatment
        # For each Treatment (column), subset where value >0.99 and count rows for Always.
        # For each Treatment (column), subset where value == 0 and count rows for Never.

        S_always[S_always <= 0.99] <- NA

        S_sometimes <- S_probfund[,2:ncol(S_probfund)] # Error in colSums(Co_never[, -1], na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric
        S_sometimes[S_sometimes == 0.00] <- NA
        S_sometimes[S_sometimes > 0.99] <- NA
        S_sometimes[!is.na(S_sometimes)] <- 1
        S_sometimes <- cbind(S_probfund[,1], S_sometimes)

        S_never[S_never != 0.00] <- NA
        S_never[S_never == 0.00] <- 1

        # How many species, for each treatment are always/never funded? Add each parameter treatment (B, Co, BCo etc), as it is completed.
        S_probfund_results<- data.frame(NULL)

        S_probfund_results<-rbind(S_always, S_sometimes, S_never)
```

```{r Co_Treatments, echo=FALSE, warning=TRUE, message=FALSE, include = FALSE}
        Co_sometimes<- colSums(Co_sometimes[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)
        Co_never<- colSums(Co_never[,-1], na.rm=TRUE)

        Co_probfund_results<-rbind(Co_always, Co_sometimes, Co_never)
        # datatable((Co_probfund_results))

system("say Co loop is finished running!")

# Write files so this doesn't always need to be rerun:
    write.csv(datasim, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/one.of.the.datasim.Co.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    write.csv(Co_probfund_results, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Co_probfund_results.csv", row.names = TRUE)
    write.csv(Co_output, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Co_output.csv", row.names = FALSE)
    write.csv(Co_probfund, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Co_probfund.csv", row.names = TRUE)

################# End Co_Treatment ################

```


## Results/Discussion
 
#### Number of Species Funded / Performance of the Funded Portfolio
 
**Table 1. Performance of the Funded Portfolios** 
This analysis investigates how uncertainty in the estimates of Benefit, Success and Feasibility change the mean number of Funded Species in the funded portfolio (i.e. sum of SpeciesInPlan for Recovery Plans where Outcome = 1), and the performance of the funded portfolio (i.e., B*S*sum SpeciesInPlan for Recovery Plans where Outcome = 1). Values presented mean +/- SD for 3 budget levels. Here SimSet = Uncertainty & Budget Treatments (HHL would translate to H = High Uncertainty for B&S + H = High Uncertainty for Co + L = Low Budget). Note that for simplicity, the same Uncertainty treatments (H, M or L) were applied to both B&S and Co parameters.

```{r Table1_Performance_Funded_Portfolios, echo = FALSE, warning = TRUE, message = FALSE, include = TRUE}
# Make Table for Report
    Output_3UBudget <- Output_3UBudget %>%
            arrange(UBS) %>%
            arrange(UBudget) %>%
            arrange(Treatment) %>%
            select(Treatment, Uncertainty, UBS, UCo, BudgetHML, UBudget, BudgetUSD, MeanFunded, SDFunded, MeanPerform, SDPerform)


    datatable(Output_3UBudget, rownames=FALSE)
    write.csv(Output_3UBudget, file="./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Table 1. MeanFunded and Performance for all combinations.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

#### Probability of Funding

The next part of the analysis looks at the PROBABILITY of funding - how uncertainty influences the probablily that a Recovery Plan (unique_plan_num, **NOT SPECIES**) will be in the funded pool. Once projects are ranked, those around the funding threshold are more likely to flip in and out when there is uncertainty (i.e., if prob fund ~50%) than those closer to the start or end of the ranked list of Recovery Plans. The data presented is the probability a Recovery Plan (unique_plan_num) was in the funded pool for a given budget, when uncertainty was introduced and the analysis was run 100 times. 
 
How could this be used? A manager could speculate on their level of uncertainty for cost, benefit or success then take the table, and use it to inform their decisions about which Recovery Plan (unique_plan_num) are always likely to be cost effective - even under high uncertainty - and choose to work on these first. 
 
 V1. I set to always/never threshold to 1 & 0 because the decision about were to put the threshold is subjective - and IMHO should be made by the decision maker. That said, I can feel confident in publishing a paper that asserts how to treat 1's and 0's. I would be inclined to leave 'always and never' as is, and perhaps add a third category of 0.99 - 0.70 as 'sometimes'?
 
Take the cumulative budget of 1s, 0.99s etc. 
Get a single prob of inclusion value for each run across all species. Reinsert the initial budget. Do the cumulative spend in order (using the average cost from the Recovery Plan). Where is the cut off point (the budget). What is the probability of inclusion for plans when you add 10% to the budget.

```{r Table2a, include=FALSE}
            melt(ind = rownames(BSCo_probfund), id.vars = "unique_plan_num", measure.vars = c("LLH", "LLM", "LLL", "MMH", "MMM", "MML", "HHH", "HHM", "HHL"))   %>%
            separate(variable, into = c("Uncertainty", "Budget"), sep = 2) %>%
                mutate(Uncertainty = ifelse(Uncertainty == "HH", "High",
                                        ifelse(Uncertainty =="MM", "Medium",
                                           ifelse(Uncertainty == "LL", "Low", "NO VALUE")))) %>%
                mutate(Budget = ifelse(Budget == "H", sim_df[1,4],
                                        ifelse(Budget =="M", sim_df[2,4],
                                           ifelse(Budget == "L", sim_df[3,4], "NO VALUE")))) %>%
                mutate(Budget = dollar(as.numeric(Budget))) %>%
            arrange(Budget, Uncertainty, unique_plan_num)

datatable(Table2a.BSCo.tidy, rownames=TRUE)

write.csv(Table2a.BSCo.tidy, file= "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Table 2a. TIDY Probability of Funding for all Treatments on BSCo.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```

 
 
Using the Probability of Funding can help to inform a managers decision about which Recovery Plans (unique_plan_num) to fund if they are not confident in the existing estimates of Recovery Cost, Benefit (degree of threat from RPNs) or Success (recoverability potential from RPNs). It is possible, given a specified budget and estimated level of uncertainty, to run the simulation and identify the subset of projects that are ‘safe bets’ or ‘risky’ (i.e., probability inclusion in the funded portfolio = 100% or 0%). 
* Safe bets: Recovery Plans that are so cost efficient that they will always be in the funded portfolio, regardless of uncertainty, so there is a very low risk in funding this species. 
* Risky bets: Recovery Plans that are so cost *in*efficient that they are never in the funded portfolio, regardless of uncertainty – so there is a very low risk in choosing not to fund these species. For projects with intermediate probabilities of funding, decisions must be made at the manager’s discretion. 
 
 
**Figure 2.**
This figure illustrates how often the Probability of Funding is 100% or 0% for Recovery Plans (unique_plan_num), and how introducing High, Medium and Low Uncertainty into the estimates of Benefit, Feasibility and Cost changes this result for all budget levels. This example highlights the large number that are always in the funded portfolio at differet uncertainty levels (i.e., ProbFund = 100) and those never in the funded pool (i.e., ProbFund = 0)

```{r sometimes_exploration_BSCo}
    Decision80.40 <- BSCo_probfund %>%
```

```{r sometimes_exploration_Co2}
                               ifelse(HHM <= 0.0, "Fund Later",
                                     ifelse(HHM < 0.9, "Flexible", NA)))) %>%
        count(Decision) %>%
        mutate(Treatment = "Min90") 
        
    Min85 <- Co_probfund %>%
        select(unique_plan_num, HHM) %>% 
        mutate(Decision = ifelse(HHM >= 0.85, "Fund Now",
                               ifelse(HHM <= 0.0, "Fund Later",
                                     ifelse(HHM < 0.85, "Flexible", NA)))) %>%
        count(Decision) %>%
        mutate(Treatment = "Min85") 
       
    Min80 <- Co_probfund %>%
        select(unique_plan_num, HHM) %>% 
        mutate(Decision = ifelse(HHM >= 0.8, "Fund Now",
                               ifelse(HHM <= 0.0, "Fund Later",
                                     ifelse(HHM < 0.8, "Flexible", NA)))) %>%
        count(Decision) %>%
        mutate(Treatment = "Min80") 
       
    Min75 <- Co_probfund %>%
        select(unique_plan_num, HHM) %>% 
        mutate(Decision = ifelse(HHM >= 0.75, "Fund Now",
                               ifelse(HHM <= 0.0, "Fund Later",
                                     ifelse(HHM < 0.75, "Flexible", NA)))) %>%
        count(Decision) %>%
        mutate(Treatment = "Min75")  

# Bind dataframes together to create a df we can graph
df<- rbind(Min100, Min95, Min90, Min85, Min80, Min75)

df <- df %>%
    filter(!is.na(Decision)) %>%
    droplevels()

# View(df)
str(df)

# # Specify order for Decisions (shouldn't be needed if done above, but here for good measure)
    df$Decision <- factor(df$Decision, levels = c("Fund Now", "Flexible", "Fund Later"))
    df$Decision2<-relevel(df$Decision, "Fund Now")
    df$Treatment <- factor(df$Treatment, levels = c("Min100", "Min95", "Min90", "Min85", "Min80", "Min75"))



# Stacked bar plot of Always/Sometimes/Never for all treatments
    # cbbPalette <- c("#99CC66","#FF9933","#993333")
    # cbbPalette <- c("green","orange","red")
    cbbPalette <- c("chartreuse4","darkorange3","firebrick")

Figure.4.HHM_Co<- ggplot(df, aes(x = Treatment, y = n , fill = Decision)) +
```

```{r Figure5B_plusminusSD_PINEAPPLE}
    arrange(unique_plan_num)


# Set up the empty dataframes for each summary result
B_results <- list()
B_mean_plansfunded <- as.numeric()
B_sd_plansfunded <- as.numeric()


# 2-level loop: Simulate uncertainty to Benefit & Cost and calculate CEA for species at multiple Budget levels
loops <-100 # Define number of loop

for (t in 1:nrow(sim_df)){
    ##  Give a 'progress bar' to see where you are in the loop
    # cat('sim_df Co',t,'/',nrow(sim_df),'\n')

    ## Create place to store results
    results_df <- list()
    results_plansfunded <- numeric()

        for(i in 1:loops) {

        # Add uncertainty to B&S at species level. For benefit, uncertainty is introduced to B_with/without_Mgmt, then B is calculated
        # datasim <- dataSpp %>%
        #     mutate( B_without_Mgmt = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$B_without_Mgmt), dataSpp$B_without_Mgmt, sim_df[t,"UBS"]),
        #             B_with_Mgmt    = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$B_with_Mgmt), dataSpp$B_with_Mgmt, sim_df[t,"UBS"]),
        #             S              = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$S), dataSpp$S, sim_df[t,"UBS"])) %>%
        #     mutate(B = B_with_Mgmt - B_without_Mgmt)

        datasim <- dataSpp %>%
            mutate( B_without_Mgmt = B_without_Mgmt,
                    B_with_Mgmt    = B_with_Mgmt,
                    S              = rBeta(1:length(dataSpp$S), dataSpp$S, sim_df[t,"UBS"])) %>%
            # mutate(B = B_with_Mgmt - B_without_Mgmt) %>% # delete this
            mutate(B = rBeta(1:length(B), B, sim_df[t,"UBS"]))

        # Get back to B&S&Co at plan level
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            group_by(unique_plan_num) %>%
            summarise(
                B = sum(B, na.rm = TRUE),
                S = mean(S, na.rm = TRUE),
                Co = mean(Co, na.rm = TRUE),
                SpeciesInPlan = mean(SpeciesInPlan, na.rm = TRUE),
                B_without_Mgmt = sum(B_without_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE), #**changed Oct 17**##
                B_with_Mgmt = sum(B_with_Mgmt, na.rm = TRUE)) #**changed Oct 17**##

        # Convert Co for total plan to ANNUAL costs (divide by 50)
        datasim <- mutate(datasim, Co=(Co/50))

        # Add uncertainty to Co at plan level
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            rowwise() %>%
            mutate(Co = rnorm(1, mean = Co, sd = Co*sim_df[t,"UCo"]))

        # print(head(datasim)) #  << CHECKS THAT relevant parameters are changing

        # Calculate cost efficiency and outcome for each plan
        datasim <- datasim %>%
            mutate(CE=((B*S)/Co)) %>%
            arrange(desc(CE)) %>%
            mutate(CumSum=cumsum(Co)) %>%
            mutate(Outcome=ifelse(CumSum >= sim_df[t,"UBudget"], 0, 1)) %>%
            arrange(unique_plan_num)

        # HOW MANY RECOVERY PLANS (not species) FUNDED per treatment?
            results_plansfunded[i] <- sum(datasim$Outcome)

        # Save each datasim as a list
        results_df[[i]] <- datasim


                # # Here we make sure that the cum cost of each funded profolio does not exceed the budget level
                # x <- datasim %>%
                #  group_by(Outcome) %>%
                #  summarise(sum = sum(Co))
                # x2 <- ifelse(x$sum[2] > sim_df[t,"UBudget"], "OH NO", "OK")
                # troubleshoot2 <- data.frame(loopi = i, loopt = t, check = x2)
                # troubleshoot <- rbind(troubleshoot,troubleshoot2)

        }

    B_mean_plansfunded[t] <- mean(results_plansfunded)
    B_sd_plansfunded[t] <- sd(results_plansfunded)
    B_results[[t]] <- results_df
}


# 1 & 2) Create dataframe to hold results for mean +/- SD # Species Funded/Performance
# Numb Funded Species & Performance for each treatment
B_output_plans <- data.frame(Treatment=rep("B", nrow(sim_df)),
                          SimSet=sim_df$SimSet,
                          UBS=sim_df$UBS,
                          UCo=sim_df$UCo,
                          UBudget=sim_df$UBudget,
                          MeanPlansFunded=round(B_mean_plansfunded,1),
                          SDPlansFunded=round(B_sd_plansfunded,2))

write.csv(B_output_plans, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/B_output_plans.csv", row.names = F)

}else{
```

## Characteristics of the datasets. 

Confidence Intervals for Benefit or Success, illustrating impact of uncertainty on estimates when Low (variance = 0.001), Medium (variance = 0.005) and High (variance = 0.01) variance is introduced using a beta distribution. Selected values reflect the scaled Min, Median and Maximum Benefit and Success values used in the prioritization of Recovery Plans.


The objective here is to report the  
- SPECIES level Benefit and Feasibility (as this is the level at which uncertainty is introduced) - for the scaled data set
- RECOVERY PLAN level Benefit and Feasiblity (as this is the level at which plans are prioritized) - for the scaled data set
- RECOVERY PLAN level Cost (as this is the only level for which we *have* this data) - also it won't be scaled

```{r TableUBS_TableCO_confidence_intervals}
# Bootstrapping confidence intervals for BENEFIT and SUCCESS from BETA distribution (0.12 - 0.88)

# It’s extremely easy to use in R, and you don’t even have to supply a density functio (https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/82475/calculate-the-confidence-interval-for-the-mean-of-a-beta-distribution)
library(simpleboot)

sim_beta<-read.csv("./data/Run 20 - Sept 2020/sim_beta.csv")

# # Set up the empty dataframes for each summary result
beta_results <- list()
beta_mean_funded <- as.numeric()
beta_sd_funded <- as.numeric()
beta_mean_perform <- as.numeric()
beta_sd_perform <- as.numeric()
beta_probfund <- data.frame(unique_plan_num = unique(dataSpp$unique_plan_num))  # UPDATED Oct 17 2017

results_sim_beta <- numeric() 

for (t in 1:nrow(sim_beta))
    {
    ##  Optional: give a 'progress bar' to see where you are in the loop
    # cat('sim_beta',t,'/',nrow(sim_beta),'\n')
    
    # results_sim_beta <- numeric()
  
    # Set up possible 1000 values given beta distribution with defined mean and variance
    
    mu <- sim_beta$mu[t]
    simasq <- sim_beta$simasq[t]
    
    a <-    alpha <-((1-sim_beta$mu[t])/sim_beta$simasq[t] - (1/sim_beta$mu[t]))*sim_beta$mu[t]^2
    b <-    beta <- (sim_beta$simasq[t] + sim_beta$mu[t]^2 - sim_beta$mu[t])*(sim_beta$mu[t] - 1)/sim_beta$simasq[t]
    n <- 1000 # how many numbers should this beta distribution have? (should be 100)
    x <- rbeta(n, alpha, beta)
    # curve(dbeta(x,alpha,beta), xlab = "Benefit or Success", ylab = "Frequency")
  
    
    # Bootstrap to get the CI using the adjusted bootstrap percentile (BCa) method, then export the min-max result https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/82475/calculate-the-confidence-interval-for-the-mean-of-a-beta-distribution
   
    x.boot = one.boot(x, mean, R=10^4)
    # hist(x.boot)                # Looks good
    result<- boot.ci(x.boot, type="bca") # Confidence interval
   
    indices <- c(4,5)
    lowerCI <- as.numeric(result$bca[indices])[1]
    upperCI <- as.numeric(result$bca[indices])[2]
    
    df <- data.frame(mu, simasq, lowerCI, upperCI)
   
    results_sim_beta <- rbind(results_sim_beta, df)
    
    }

# Rearrange data into table format

results_sim_beta2 <- results_sim_beta %>%
    mutate(ConfidenceInterval = paste(round(lowerCI,3), "-", round(upperCI,3))) %>%
    mutate( lowerCI = round(lowerCI,3),
            upperCI = round(upperCI,3),
            variance = simasq) %>%
    select(-lowerCI, -upperCI, -simasq)

TableUBSCI <- spread(results_sim_beta2, mu, ConfidenceInterval) 

TableUBSCI

print("Table 1: The minimum and maximum of random values drawn from a beta distribution, illustrating impact of uncertainty on estimates of benefit and success when Low (variance = 0.001), Medium (variance = 0.005) and High (variance = 0.01) levels of uncertainty are introduced.")

write.csv(TableUBSCI, file = "./output/Run 20 - Sept 2020/Table UBS. Confidence Intervals for Benefit or Success.csv")
```
